summary: Most of the reviewer's findings hold. Five needed corrections. (1) The JS comparison was a cache artifact: lessons and the curriculum ship about 330 KB gzipped, the same as the home page. The real home-page problem is 15 elements served at opacity:0. (2) The site has ten themes (five palettes in light and dark), and the dark palettes share one slate surface set, which explains the borderless fields in sunset-dark. (3) The sidebar quick links are deliberate below xl. (4) Settings already has the palette picker. (5) Reusing the Navbar needs the learning providers. The tap-target finding was dropped: none of the targets fails WCAG 2.5.8 AA. Finding 15 was widened: there is no OG image or app icon either. No separate new findings were needed.
strengths: Lesson wayfinding is excellent: the breadcrumb, a course outline with mono module codes and the current lesson highlighted, the 'On this page' TOC with an active state and EXPERT tags, and 'Lesson 1 of 1 / module 1 of 14' plus 'Builds toward: M0' context (lesson-f1a.desktop.default-dark.s0.png).

Trust signals are strong: sourced statistics (2022 Wilson Research Group), IEEE clause citations, 'Deterministic educational model' and 'Assumptions and limits' badges on interactives, and honest 'Your progress is saved in this browser' notes.

The UVM phasing visual (viz-uvm-phasing.desktop.default-dark.s0.png) is the most distinctive design on the site, with mono phase chips, labelled lanes and direction arrows. It should seed the visual identity.
JetBrains Mono is used well for code and module codes, and the Monaco token colours were tuned for contrast (src/lib/monaco-themes.ts comments).
No horizontal overflow on any captured page (metrics.json overflowX 0). Mobile has a working drawer, a search button and a collapsible 'On this page' summary ('27 sections, 6 expert').
The Knowledge Hub module map (knowledge-hub.desktop.default-dark.s0.png) is a clear, keyboard-operable lane diagram with mono module codes, the same instrument-like language as the phasing visual.
The 404 page is helpful: it shows the requested address, recovery links and search tips with real module-code examples.
Copy in the app shell is specific and learner-oriented (placement quiz: 'Ten questions, about six minutes'; dashboard: 'Stored only in this browser').
The privacy and terms pages already have a minimal header (Logo plus 'Back to the curriculum'), at src/app/(public)/privacy-policy/page.tsx:113-131. It is a ready pattern for the landing page.
proposal:
Direction A, "Bench instrument" (recommended). Verification engineers spend their days in waveform viewers, logs and spec PDFs. The site should feel like a well-made instrument for that work: precise, quiet and data-literate.
Type: a text sans for body and UI. The Inter 400/700 files are already bundled; IBM Plex Sans is an option. JetBrains Mono stays for code, module codes, signal names and labels. Cal Sans is kept only for h1 and the wordmark. Today body text asks for weight 400, but the only Cal Sans file is SemiBold (600), so all text renders SemiBold and bold text is synthesised.
Colour: neutral off-white ink on navy, one interaction colour (cyan), and waveform-style state colours used sparingly: green for pass, amber for X or warning, red for fail. Mint becomes the 'current' marker only. Each palette must also define its own surface tokens (card, muted, border, input). Today all dark palettes share the same slate set, which is why cards look pasted on and fields lose their borders in sunset-dark.
Dark and light: one palette in two modes. Dark is deep navy with off-white text; light is cool white with navy ink and a cyan-700 primary. Retire Ocean, Sunset, Forest and Violet (eight of the ten themes), or keep one high-contrast mode. The palette select already lives in /settings (SettingsPageClient.tsx:96), so the Navbar keeps only the light/dark toggle.
Landing: a header on top, either the privacy page's minimal header extended with search and the main links, or the full Navbar once the public layout has the providers it needs. A left-aligned headline with real counts, rendered as static server markup. A static crop of the UVM phasing map or the Knowledge Hub lane map as the hero visual. Then the three routes, then real thumbnails of four interactives. No eyebrow chip, halo, icon tiles or rotating tagline.
Lesson page: no card around the prose. The reading column sits on the page background at about 70ch. Mono module codes in the outline and breadcrumb. Only callouts, interactives, labs and quizzes are boxed, each with a hairline border and a mono label ('TESTED MODEL', 'EXPERT'). The right-hand TOC stays as it is.

Direction B, "Engineering handbook": a light-first technical book, with a serif body, a sans for UI, sidenotes for IEEE citations and interactives numbered as figures. It suits long reading for juniors, but it means restyling about 118 interactives and moves the site away from the tools experts use.

Recommendation: Direction A. It fits the audience's tools and mental models, reuses the site's most distinctive pieces (the phasing map, the module-map lanes, mono codes and the model badges), and keeps dark mode first-class. Most of the work is tokens in globals.css, a font-stack change in tailwind.config.ts, one PageHeader, removing the prose card in the lesson page, and a static hero.

findings.title: Every word, lesson body and diagrams included, renders in one display face at SemiBold (Cal Sans 600)
findings.evidence: fonts.ts:46-52 loads only public/fonts/CalSans-SemiBold.otf (weight 600) as --font-cal-sans. tailwind.config.ts:54-59 puts var(--font-cal-sans) first in fontFamily.sans, and layout.tsx:28 puts font-sans on body. Inter 400/700 (fonts.ts:10-26) is preloaded but only ever acts as a fallback. metrics.json: body font is __calSans at 16px/24px with declared weight 400 on all 64 page loads. Because the only face is 600, the browser renders 400 text at SemiBold, and font-bold/strong (700) is synthesised. Screenshots: in lesson-f1a.desktop.default-dark.s0.png the 'What it is:' bold lead-ins barely differ from the body. In lesson-f1a.desktop.default-dark.s1.png the inline SVG diagram labels ('spec review', 'RTL simulation') are also Cal Sans.
findings.impact: Long lessons (75-minute reads) are tiring to read, and emphasis cannot be told apart from body text. All 112 lessons and every page look like a marketing hero instead of a technical reference.
findings.fix: In tailwind.config.ts set fontFamily.sans to [var(--font-inter), system-ui, sans-serif] and add fontFamily.display = [var(--font-cal-sans), var(--font-inter), sans-serif]. In the globals.css base layer apply font-display to h1 (and h2 if wanted). Logo.tsx already sets var(--font-cal-sans) itself. Optionally add an Inter 600 file for UI labels, and convert CalSans-SemiBold.otf to woff2. After the swap, recheck prose line-height and measure, and recheck diagram label widths.
tests: No unit tests pin font families (grep for cal-sans/font-inter in tests/ finds nothing). Playwright visual checks in tests/e2e/regression-gates.spec.ts should be re-run because text metrics change.

findings.title: Default dark uses neon mint as the base text colour, and mint and cyan compete as heading/accent colours
findings.evidence: globals.css:73 sets --foreground: 165 100% 70% (#64FFDA). Line 75 sets --accent to the same mint, and line 74 sets --primary to cyan #00BFFF. Anything using text-foreground or text-foreground/N turns mint: there are 58 text-foreground/N uses in src. In home.desktop.default-dark.s2.png the card descriptions and the section lead are mint body copy, while the h2 'Experience Interactive Learning' and the card h3s are cyan (text-primary, lines 53 and 76). 'Choose your route' in s1 is mint. On the lesson, the h1 is mint and the 'Quick Take' h2 is white (card-foreground). On viz-uvm-phasing the h1 is white and the 'Diagrams & Illustrations' h2 is cyan. In the sidebar, the mint quick links are not underlined, while the cyan 'Open F1A' link on the Knowledge Hub is.
findings.impact: Saturated neon body copy is harsh in a dark room. Heading colours change from page to page with no rule. Mint is used both for plain text and for links, so link affordance is unclear.
findings.fix: In globals.css default-dark, set --foreground to an off-white (for example 210 25% 90%) and keep --accent mint only for state (done, current). Make headings text-foreground everywhere. In InteractiveFeaturesSection change the h2/h3 from text-primary to text-foreground and the copy from text-foreground/80 to text-muted-foreground. Keep cyan (primary) for links and buttons.
tests: No tests pin the colour tokens. Re-run tests/e2e/theming.spec.ts and any axe contrast checks in tests/e2e/regression-gates.spec.ts.

findings.title: Default light and dark look like two brands, and ten themes (five palettes) dilute the identity
findings.where: src/app/globals.css:18-21 (root light), 37-62 (default-light), 64-89 (default-dark), 91-255 (ocean, sunset, forest and violet, light and dark); src/components/ui/ThemeSwitcher.tsx:13-17; src/components/Navbar.tsx:578
findings.evidence: home.desktop.default-light.s0.png: a cream #FDF8F0 background with crimson #DB0037 used for the wordmark and active nav. home.desktop.default-dark.s0.png: navy with mint and cyan. ThemeSwitcher.tsx:13-17 offers five palettes (Default, Ocean, Sunset, Forest, Violet), and each has a light and a dark variant: ten themes. Each palette changes only --background, --foreground, --primary and --accent. Card, muted, secondary, border and input are identical across all dark palettes (for example --card 222.2 84% 4.9% everywhere), so lesson-f1a.desktop.sunset-dark.s0.png shows near-black navy cards on a slate page. The Navbar renders the palette select (Navbar.tsx:578), and /settings renders the same ThemeSwitcher (SettingsPageClient.tsx:96).
findings.impact: A learner who toggles the mode, or a colleague opening a shared link, sees a different-looking product. Every palette is another set of contrast pairs to keep at AA across about 118 interactives.
findings.fix: Derive default-light from the dark palette's hues: cool white background, navy ink, cyan-700 primary, teal-700 for state. Retire the other four palettes, or keep a single high-contrast mode. Remove ThemeSwitcher from Navbar.tsx (it stays in settings) and keep the sun/moon toggle. Migrate stored palette values in ThemeProvider to default-light or default-dark.

findings.title: The landing hero background ends in hard vertical edges at the container sides
findings.evidence: page.tsx:32 sets main to 'flex flex-col items-center', so the hero <section> (HeroSection.tsx:44, no w-full) shrinks to its max-w-6xl child (1152px). Its absolute inset-x-0 gradient (line 46) and blur halo (line 50) are clipped by overflow-hidden at that width. home.desktop.default-dark.s0.png shows sharp vertical edges at x=144 and x=1296 for the top ~250px, and default-light and violet-dark show the same.
findings.impact: The first thing a visitor sees looks broken, which costs trust in the first second.
findings.fix: Add w-full to the section className at HeroSection.tsx:44, or drop items-center from main at page.tsx:32. Better, delete the halo div at line 50 as part of design-critic-6.

findings.title: The landing page has no site header: no wordmark, navigation, search or theme control
findings.evidence: home.desktop.default-dark.s0.png and home.mobile.default-dark.s0.png start directly with the eyebrow chip. The only ways in are the two hero buttons, the route cards and the footer three screens down. The privacy and terms pages in the same route group do have a header (privacy-policy/page.tsx:113-131: Logo plus 'Back to the curriculum'), so the home page is the only public page without one. The full Navbar depends on useAuth and useOutlineToggle (Navbar.tsx:8,15), which come from the (learning) ClientProviders.
findings.impact: A returning learner cannot search or jump to Labs from the front door, and the landing page feels like a separate site.
findings.fix: Smallest change: render the privacy page's header in page.tsx, extended with Curriculum, Practice, Labs and Dashboard links and a SearchCombobox trigger. Factor it into src/components/layout/PublicHeader.tsx and reuse it on privacy and terms. Alternative: give Navbar a hideOutlineToggle prop and wrap (public)/layout.tsx in the providers it needs.

findings.title: The landing page serves 15 elements, the h1 included, at opacity:0 until framer-motion hydrates
findings.evidence: curl -s https://sv-uvm-guide.rakesh-n99.workers.dev/ | grep -o 'opacity:0;transform:translateY([0-9-]*px)' | sort | uniq -c returns 15 elements with inline opacity:0: the hero wrapper, h1, tagline, skills card, highlights, section headings, four feature cards and the route cards. metrics.json: home lcpMs is 2048 on desktop and 2728 on mobile. Correction: the reviewer's '332 KB vs about 10 KB elsewhere' is a cache artifact. The capture reused one browser context and home loaded first. Measured cold with curl, gzipped JS is 253 KB for /, 338 KB for /curriculum and 331 KB for the F1A lesson. Other pages' LCP figures are also warm-cache, so the LCP gap is overstated, but the hidden h1 is real. home.desktop.default-dark.s1.png shows 'Not sure which route fits?' captured mid-fade, and in s2 the fourth feature card sits about 3px low because of its staggered whileInView delay (index*0.1), not because its title is taller.
findings.impact: On a slow phone the hero is blank until about 250 KB of JS runs. Content is also invisible to anyone whose JS fails, and scroll-in fades make the page feel unfinished.
findings.fix: Render the hero h1, support line, CTAs and the section headings and cards as plain server markup with no initial opacity. If motion is wanted, use a CSS keyframe on secondary elements under motion-safe:. Drop framer-motion from HeroSection and InteractiveFeaturesSection so both can be server components, once the tagline rotation goes (design-critic-6).

findings.title: The hero reads as a generic template: eyebrow chip, radial halo, stock headline, rotating tagline
findings.evidence: The tagline array (lines 11-16) includes 'From Basics to Brilliance in UVM' and 'The Ultimate Open-Source UVM Learning Hub', and rotates every 5 s (setInterval, lines 36-41). The rounded-full chip at line 60 reads 'Complete SV/UVM roadmap'. A blur-3xl halo sits at line 50. The headline 'Master SystemVerilog & UVM with confidence' (line 70) could belong to any course. Compare the precise, sourced voice of lesson-f1a.desktop.default-dark.s0.png. layout.tsx:14 also calls the site 'The definitive online platform'.
findings.impact: The site's real difference, accurate and sourced teaching with tested interactive models, is hidden behind copy that sounds like every course landing page. Expert visitors judge the site in seconds.
findings.fix: Replace the headline with a specific claim, for example 'SystemVerilog, UVM and AMBA verification, from your first testbench to sign-off'. Use one static support line with real counts taken from curriculumData and getAllLabs, not hard-coded. Delete the taglines, the chip and the halo. Add one real artefact, for example a static crop of the UVM phasing map. Tone down the metadata description in layout.tsx.

findings.title: 'Experience Interactive Learning' is four identical icon-tile cards with 'Try It Now' buttons
findings.evidence: home.desktop.default-dark.s2.png shows four equal cards. Each has a grey icon band (bg-muted/60 h-24, line 49) holding a lucide icon, a cyan title, mint body text and the same outline 'Try It Now' button (line 57). The 3px offset of the fourth card is an animation artifact (see design-critic-10), not a layout bug.
findings.impact: The strongest selling point, tested interactive models, is shown with clip-art icons instead of the real visuals the site already has.
findings.fix: Replace the icon band with a static SVG or screenshot thumbnail of each interactive, saved in public/visuals/. Give each card a named CTA ('Step through one delta cycle', 'Open the UVM map'). Show the 'tested model' or 'illustration' badge on each card.
tests: No test references 'Try It Now' (grep tests/). tests/app/home-page.test.tsx renders the page.

findings.title: Page container widths and page-header patterns change on almost every learning page
findings.where: src/components/layout/MainLayout.tsx:23 plus the per-page wrappers in curriculum, practice, dashboard, knowledge-hub, interview-prep, placement-quiz and not-found
findings.evidence: MainLayout.tsx:23 wraps everything in 'container mx-auto px-4', and each page then adds its own max-w and hero treatment. Left edge of the h1 at 1440px: curriculum about x=112 with no card; practice x=177 inside a boxed hero card (practice.desktop.default-dark.s0.png); dashboard about x=145 with pill sub-tabs; knowledge hub x=208 with no card (knowledge-hub.desktop.default-dark.s0.png); interview prep inside a card running about 272-1168; viz-uvm-phasing in a slate card with a white h1 and a cyan h2 (viz-uvm-phasing.desktop.default-dark.s0.png). The lesson page uses max-w-6xl (curriculum/[...slug]/page.tsx:106). src/components/templates/InfoPage.tsx already provides a consistent header for the legal pages.
findings.impact: Each section looks like a different template, and the layout shifts as learners move between pages.
findings.fix: Create src/components/layout/PageHeader.tsx (optional eyebrow, h1, lead, actions, sub-nav), modelled on InfoPage. Define two widths: reading (about max-w-3xl) and wide (max-w-7xl). Apply them to every (learning) index page and remove the per-page hero cards and ad-hoc max-w classes.

findings.title: Lesson pages box everything: the breadcrumb, the header and the whole prose body are rounded cards
findings.evidence: Breadcrumbs.tsx:29 gives the breadcrumb 'rounded-2xl border bg-card/60'. The lesson header is a second card (LessonOrientation). page.tsx:134 wraps the whole MDX article in 'prose ... rounded-3xl border border-border/60 bg-card/70 p-4 sm:p-6'. In lesson-f1a.desktop.default-dark.s0.png there are three stacked cards above the fold. lesson-f1a.mobile.default-dark.s0.png shows the same inside the 16px page gutter.
findings.impact: Card borders add noise around long reading text and cost about 32px of width on a 390px phone. Real callouts ('Before you start', interactives) stop standing out because everything is boxed.
findings.fix: Remove rounded-3xl, border, bg-card/70 and the padding from the article at page.tsx:134. Render the breadcrumb as a plain text row (Breadcrumbs.tsx:29) and the LessonOrientation header on the page background. Keep card chrome only for interactives, labs, callouts and quizzes. Consider a max-w-[72ch] reading column.

findings.title: Dark palettes share one slate surface set, so sunset-dark fields lose their borders and cards clash
findings.where: src/app/globals.css:153-171 (sunset-dark) and the other dark palettes (112-130, 194-212, 235-253)
findings.evidence: sunset-dark sets --background: 215 28% 17% (line 154), while its --border and --input are 217.2 32.6% 17.5% (lines 168-169), essentially the same colour. In lesson-f1a.desktop.sunset-dark.s0.png the 'Search lessons...' field and the 'Sunset' select have no visible boundary, and the cards are the shared near-black navy (--card 222.2 84% 4.9%) on a slate page. default-dark and forest-light keep visible borders.
findings.impact: In that theme the search box is hard to recognise as a field (WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast), and in all dark palettes except default the cards look pasted on.
findings.fix: Retire the extra palettes as part of design-critic-3. If they stay, give each palette its own --card, --muted, --border and --input derived from its background, with borders at 3:1 or better against the header.

findings.title: The product has two names: 'SV/UVM Hub' in the UI and 'SV/UVM Mastery' in titles and metadata
findings.where: src/components/ui/Logo.tsx:10,20; src/components/Navbar.tsx:534; src/components/Footer.tsx:125; privacy-policy/page.tsx:117; terms-of-service/page.tsx:122 vs src/app/layout.tsx:11-19; src/server/ai/index.ts:12
findings.evidence: The wordmark, the aria-labels and the footer copyright say 'SV/UVM Hub'. layout.tsx:11-19 uses the default title 'SystemVerilog & UVM Mastery', the template '%s | SV/UVM Mastery' and siteName 'SV/UVM Mastery', and CHAT_POLICY says 'SV/UVM Mastery tutor'. Every metrics.json title ends in '| SV/UVM Mastery'.
findings.impact: Tabs, search results and shared links show a different name from the page, which weakens recall and trust.
findings.fix: Pick one name, export it as SITE_NAME from src/lib/site-links.ts, and use it in layout.tsx metadata, Logo.tsx, Navbar.tsx, Footer.tsx, the legal pages and CHAT_POLICY.

findings.title: No brand mark, app icon or social preview image: the wordmark is plain text and only a favicon.ico exists
findings.where: src/components/ui/Logo.tsx; src/app/favicon.ico; src/app (no icon, apple-icon or opengraph-image files)
findings.evidence: Logo.tsx is an SVG <text> node 'SV/UVM Hub' in hsl(var(--primary)): cyan in dark and crimson in light, on every desktop screenshot. ls src/app shows only favicon.ico. There is no icon.svg, apple-icon.png or opengraph-image, and layout.tsx openGraph has no images, so shared links show no preview card.
findings.impact: Nothing visual identifies the site in a tab, a bookmark or a shared link in a team chat.
findings.fix: Design a small mark from the domain, for example a clock-edge or square-wave glyph or a mono [SV]. Add it to Logo.tsx, src/app/icon.svg and apple-icon.png, plus src/app/opengraph-image.tsx (static, via next/og) showing the mark and the headline.

findings.title: Route-card buttons wrap on the Junior card only, and labels differ between landing and curriculum
findings.evidence: LearningPathCard.tsx:57 already uses 'mt-auto flex flex-wrap'. In home.desktop.default-dark.s1.png the Junior primary 'Begin the Junior route' plus 'See the Junior route' is wider than the card, so the buttons wrap onto two rows while the other two cards keep one row. The primaries are 'Begin the Junior route', 'Find your level' and 'Expert layers' (learning-paths.ts:170,443). The secondary is 'See the X route' on the landing (LearningPathCard.tsx:63) and 'Follow the X route' on the curriculum overview (RouteChooser.tsx:70).
findings.impact: Learners comparing routes cannot tell at a glance whether the buttons do the same thing.
findings.fix: Use parallel, short labels: primary 'Start: <first step>' from learning-paths.ts and secondary 'All steps', shared by LearningPathCard and RouteChooser. Or stack both buttons full-width on every card so the rows match.

findings.title: The lab code editor uses Monaco's default grey #1e1e1e, which clashes with the navy shell
findings.evidence: The dark theme (base vs-dark) sets token rules and line-number colours but no 'editor.background' (grep finds none). lab-basics.desktop.default-dark.s0.png shows a neutral grey editor panel inside the navy (#0A192F) page and next to the navy step sidebar.
findings.impact: The most hands-on surface on the site looks pasted in from another app.
findings.fix: Add colors 'editor.background', 'editorGutter.background', 'editor.lineHighlightBackground' and 'minimap.background' in a navy matching --card or --background. The token colours were tuned to AA against #1e1e1e and the highlighted line, so re-measure them against the new background (comments at lines 55-57) and do the same for the light theme.

findings.title: Three hero highlight cards in a two-column grid leave an orphan and repeat the route cards' message
findings.evidence: In home.desktop.default-dark.s0.png 'Reusable playbooks' sits alone in the left column under two cards, with empty space to its right (grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2, line 118).
findings.impact: The first viewport looks unbalanced and unfinished.
findings.fix: Delete the highlights block, since the route cards below say the same more specifically. If it stays, use sm:grid-cols-3.

findings.title: On mobile the lesson breadcrumb wraps to two lines inside a card
findings.evidence: In lesson-f1a.mobile.default-dark.s0.png 'Curriculum > Tier 1: Foundations' is on one line and '> F1A: The Cost of Bugs' on a second, inside a card about 85px tall (the ol uses flex-wrap, line 34). The h1 directly below repeats the current crumb.
findings.impact: It uses up the top of the mobile screen and looks broken.
findings.fix: Below sm, render only a back link to the parent ('< Tier 1: Foundations'), with the full trail from sm up, and drop the card chrome (design-critic-9).

findings.title: From xl up, the sidebar's pinned quick links repeat the navbar links and shrink the outline
findings.where: src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx:39-52 (OUTLINE_QUICK_LINKS) and where the quick-links list is rendered
findings.evidence: In lesson-f1a.desktop.default-dark.s0.png the bottom-left block lists 'Start here, Curriculum overview, Practice hub, Labs, Interview prep, Dashboard' in mint, while the navbar above shows the same links. The block is pinned, so the outline scrolls above it and F4C is cut at the fold; it does not cover rows. The comment at Sidebar.tsx:39-43 says this is deliberate because the navbar shows Labs, Interview prep and Dashboard only from xl. Below xl the block is needed.
findings.impact: On wide screens it adds noise and takes about 100px from the course outline, the sidebar's main job.
findings.fix: Add xl:hidden to the desktop quick-links list in Sidebar.tsx. Keep it in the mobile drawer and below xl.
tests: tests/components/Sidebar.test.tsx (quick links tests near lines 212 and 314)

dropped.reason: Not a WCAG failure, and it belongs to the responsive-a11y lens. The 40px threshold is a heuristic. Every cited target passes WCAG 2.5.8 AA (24x24 or adequate spacing): the logo is 128x26 and the resources chips are 30px tall. The 20px assessment items are inline text links in a list with space-y-4 (AssessmentPageClient.tsx:123-128), which satisfies the spacing exception. 'Practice Hub 90x19' and 'lab steps 300x20' were not in the metrics samples I checked.
